author: followedforgo
quote: I waited 13 **** years for this ****. Thirteen years of rumours, leaks, trailers and hype. I preordered it, paid $125 AUD for the standard edition on PS5, and counted down the days like everyone else. Now I'm about halfway through, and this is the most disappointed I've ever been in a game. I wanted a crime fantasy and got a life simulator. I play games to get away from reality, not to go back into the same **** with better **** don't really play this game, you obey it. Everything revolves around Lucia. Her needs come first, her storyline comes first, and Jason follows along like he's lucky to be there. Sure, you can technically ignore her, but the game punishes you for it, so it's not really a choice. You're constantly unloading her groceries, buying her flowers and keeping her happy. After a few hours it feels like I'm being trained to say "yes dear." It should be called Simp Sim **** worst of all are the scenes where nothing happens. Sometimes you literally just watch Jason and Lucia watch TV and watch Jason rub Lucia's feet like a good little slave. This is the series where you used to rob banks, blow things up and cause chaos across an entire city. Now I'm sitting through foot rubs that go on forever. I spent more time watching long, boring scenes than playing the game I paid for. Then there's the "realism." Somebody at Rockstar decided GTA fans really wanted to shop for groceries. You come home from work in real life, turn on the game, and start working all over again: errands, chores, upkeep, relationship stuff. I already have a real life with real chores, and it doesn't cost $125. When I do try to have fun the old-fashioned way, the game stops me. I tried to steal a car, the woman inside had a panic attack, and the game wouldn't let me take it. Let that sink in. In a game literally called Grand Theft Auto, I couldn't steal a car because a woman had a tantrum. That sums up everything wrong here. The core of the series has been sanded down so nobody gets upset. That's why there's barely any real action. Chores, cutscenes and relationship maintenance keep slowing you down, and when action does come, it feels like a break from the real game, which is apparently being a good boyfriend. And it isn't funny. GTA used to be crude, vulgar and hilarious, offensive in a way that made you laugh out loud. The radio, the side characters, the satire. GTA 6 took the safe route. There's no vulgar humour and nothing that made me laugh, like it was written by people terrified of offending anyone.This is where it lost me completely. The whole game feels like it was made by women who hate men. Jason works, takes orders and puts up with everything, and the game wants you to see that as the ideal. It feels like the people who made it want men to be slaves: do the chores, keep her happy, never get angry. GTA used to be a power fantasy. This one feels like a **** characters don't help. Michael, Franklin and Trevor from GTA 5 were chaotic, funny and unpredictable. Trevor alone had more personality than this entire cast. GTA 6's characters just ****, and halfway through I still don't care about any of them.I'll give it one thing: the graphics are quite beautiful. But that doesn't make up for all the bad. It's locked at 30 FPS on console, not even the PS5 Pro gets more, and paying $125 for 30 frames per second in 2026 is absolutely horrible. The driving is horrible too, which is unforgivable in a series where you spend so much time behind the wheel.There's also no online and no co-op. Nothing. GTA Online kept GTA 5 alive for over a decade and came out two weeks after launch. GTA 6 is single-player only, and Rockstar hasn't even given a date for online. You can't even escape the boyfriend simulator by jumping into a lobby with your friends.People will point to the nearly $4 billion it made on launch day. But that's mostly preorders from people like me who bought into 13 years of hype before knowing what we'd get. Sales show how good the marketing was, not the game. And for a game that reportedly cost well over a billion dollars to make, with estimates running into the billions, this is what we got.Then there's the media. Rolling Stone ran a piece tagged "Chudpocalypse" about gamers who don't like being forced to be nice to their girlfriend. Newsweek wrote that in GTA 6, "the ultimate male fantasy is being a good boyfriend." Not liking a game's design doesn't make you a chud or mean you want to disrespect women in real life. It's a video game called Grand Theft Auto. I didn't wait 13 years for a relationship lesson. I wanted Grand Theft Auto. It's beautiful, expensive and hollow. Rockstar made a game that seems to look down on the people who've bought GTA for almost 30 years, a life simulator when people wanted a crime sandbox. If you want to do chores, follow orders and rub someone's feet, real life does that for free. Do yourself a favour and play GTA 5 again.
